summary: This script checks whether functions in Bash files within a given folder are declared in alphabetical order. It compares each file's actual function declaration order against a sorted version and displays any mismatches side-by-side so developers can see which files need their functions reordered.

explanations.5: The $# variable holds the number of arguments passed to the script; this checks that exactly one argument was provided, otherwise shows usage and exits.
explanations.12: This uses the && and && chain to: check if the folder doesn't exist, print an error message if so, and exit with code 1 (all in one line).
explanations.18: pushd changes into that directory and >/dev/null suppresses the usual output that shows the directory stack.
explanations.20: set +e turns off the 'exit on error' mode so the script keeps running even if a diff command reports differences (non-zero exit code).
explanations.23: The ! before result= means 'if the diff command fails (returns non-zero)', which happens when there are differences between the two sides.
explanations.24: <(...) is process substitution—it runs the command inside and feeds its output as if it were a file, so diff can compare two streams.
explanations.25: The right side does the same grep but pipes to sort, so it shows what the function order should be alphabetically.
explanations.31: set -e turns 'exit on error' back on so any failures after this point will stop the script.
